Fast Cox Proportional Hazards Model

Source: R/coxphGPU.R
coxphGPU.Rd

Fits a Cox proportional hazards model on the GPU (or the CPU), with the interface of survival::coxph(). Only point estimates are computed: call bootstrap() on the result for bootstrap confidence intervals, and inspect it with summary().

coxphGPU(formula, data, ties = c("efron", "breslow"), init, control,
         singular.ok = TRUE, model = FALSE, x = FALSE, y = TRUE,
         patient_id = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'coxphGPU'
summary(object, ..., conf.int = 0.95, scale = 1)

Arguments

formula

A formula with a survival object (see survival::Surv()) on the left of ~ and the terms on the right.

data

a data.frame in which to interpret the variables named in the formula, or in the subset and the weights argument.

ties

a character string specifying the method for tie handling. If there are no tied death times all the methods are equivalent. The Efron approximation is used as the default, it is more accurate when dealing with tied death times, and is as efficient computationally. (But see below for multi-state models.) The “exact partial likelihood” is equivalent to a conditional logistic model, and is appropriate when the times are a small set of discrete values.

init

vector of initial values of the iteration. Default initial value is zero for all variables.

control

Object of class coxph.control specifying iteration limit and other control options. Default is coxph.control(...).

singular.ok

logical value indicating how to handle collinearity in the model matrix. If TRUE, the program will automatically skip over columns of the X matrix that are linear combinations of earlier columns. In this case the coefficients for such columns will be NA, and the variance matrix will contain zeros. For ancillary calculations, such as the linear predictor, the missing coefficients are treated as zeros.

model

logical value: if TRUE, the model frame is returned in component model.

x

logical value: if TRUE, the x matrix is returned in component x.

y

logical value: if TRUE, the response vector is returned in component y.

patient_id

Name of the column of data that identifies each patient (subject). Required by bootstrap(), which resamples patients rather than rows, so that all the rows of a patient (e.g. with time-varying covariates) are kept together. With one row per patient, a column of row indices (data$id <- seq_len(nrow(data))) can be used.

...

For coxphGPU(): device ("cpu" or "cuda"; default: the GPU if one is available), double_precision (TRUE, the default, for 64-bit floats; FALSE for 32-bit floats, faster on most GPUs), and arguments of survival::coxph.control() (e.g. iter.max). For the methods: not used.

object

A coxphGPU object.

conf.int

level for computation of the confidence intervals. If set to FALSE no confidence intervals are printed

scale

vector of scale factors for the coefficients, defaults to 1. The printed coefficients, se, and confidence intervals will be associated with one scale unit.

Value

coxphGPU() returns an object of class coxphGPU, with the components of a survival::coxph() fit (coefficients, variance, log-likelihood, ...). With patient_id, it also contains patient_id (the column name) and patient_ids (the patient of each row used by the model).

summary() returns an object of class summary.coxphGPU, with confidence intervals for the hazard ratios from the normal approximation and, if bootstrap() was called on the model, from the bootstrap. Its main components are:

  • conf.int: matrix with one row per coefficient and the confidence limits of exp(coef).

  • conf.int_bootstrap: the same limits, from the bootstrap.

  • logtest, sctest, waldtest: likelihood ratio, score and Wald tests of the model.

  • concordance: concordance statistic and its standard error.

  • rsq: approximate \(R^2\) of Nagelkerke (Biometrika, 1991).

Details

To compute bootstrap confidence intervals with bootstrap(), fit the model with both x = TRUE, which stores the design matrix, and patient_id, which stores the patient of each row used by the model. The bootstrap then resamples exactly the data the model was fitted on.

References

Therneau T (2026). A Package for Survival Analysis in R. R package version 3.8-9, https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=survival. coxphGPU() follows the interface of its coxph(), calls it for the model frame and the martingale residuals, and is tested against it.

Therneau TM, Grambsch PM (2000). Modeling Survival Data: Extending the Cox Model. Springer, New York.

See also

survival::coxph(), bootstrap()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(survival)
library(WCE)
data(drugdata)

## Check CUDA drivers (if FALSE you use CPU)
use_cuda()

## Cox Proportional Hazards point estimate; x = TRUE and patient_id are
## required if you plan to call bootstrap() on the result afterwards.
fit <- coxphGPU(Surv(Start, Stop, Event) ~ sex + age,
                data = drugdata, x = TRUE, patient_id = "Id")

## Bootstrap-based inference, as a separate step
fit_boot <- bootstrap(fit, R = 1000,
                      batchsize = if (use_cuda()) 200 else 10)

summary(fit_boot)
} # }
